id: GB-01 path forms: drive, MSYS, UNC and non-ASCII paths under Git Bash's perl
note: Sitting 4, P1 and P4. util::posix_form reads a path another program printed (git's toplevel, git dir and worktree list, a .git file's gitdir line, a transcript's cwd) in this platform's form: under MSYS or Cygwin perl a drive form (C:/x, C:\x) through util::root_form, anything else as it is. util::root_form gives Cygwin::win_to_posix_path bytes only, and ASCII only: on the PC the real sub ended perl with 'Out of memory!' on a UTF8-flagged non-ASCII drive path, which no eval catches. A non-ASCII path converts its leading ASCII folders through the sub and keeps the rest as it is; the answer is characters only for a character input. FakeXS.pm stands in for the sub on any host (C: reads as $TMP/cyg/c) and ends perl as the PC did: on a flagged string (FAKE_XS_ABORT=flagged) or on any non-ASCII input (nonascii, the other outcome of the PC probe). On macOS or Linux nothing changes: a drive form is no root and posix_form gives every path back as it is.
